claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure containing an fcc matrix and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
The fcc matrix in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
The C14 Laves phase in FeCoNiTi is Ti-rich.
Coexistence with the C14 phase suppresses saturation magnetization relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Coexistence with the C14 phase raises coercivity significantly above the approximately 100 Oe single-phase fcc FeCoNi limit, with a target of about 667 Oe at 400 K.
The Fe, Co, and Ni moments associated with the fcc phase couple antiferromagnetically to a Ti-rich sublattice in the C14 phase or to Ti atoms at the interface.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling induces antiparallel alignment or magnetic frustration and thereby lowers the net magnetic moment of the fcc phase.
The Ti-rich C14 phase constitutes a non-magnetic or antiferromagnetic sublattice.
C14 precipitates or regions pin magnetic domain walls because of their distinct structure, chemistry, and interfacial strain.
Domain-wall pinning by the C14 phase produces the proposed increase in coercivity.
The orbital moment of the fcc phase is intrinsically limited.
Proximity to the Ti-rich C14 phase further suppresses the orbital moment of the fcc phase.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys have coercivity capped at approximately 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments and the absence of strong pinning centers.
The strength of the proposed magnetic effect depends on Ti partitioning, C14 morphology, phase distribution, and interface structure.
The effect may diminish when the C14 phase fraction is too low or when the C14 phase transforms at elevated temperature.
A coherent or semi-coherent fcc/C14 interface can mediate both magnetic coupling and domain-wall pinning.
Comparing a dual-phase alloy with a C14-dominant or single-phase fcc alloy can isolate phase-specific magnetic contributions.
Spin-polarized DFT comparing isolated fcc FeCoNiTi with an fcc/C14 interface model can test whether the interface changes the spin density of states and magnetic moment at the Fermi level.
